runtime.command_template: python tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <libpinmame> --game <driver> --rom-path <vpinmame-roms> --work-dir <new-isolated-state> --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/stern/<scenario>.json --output <external-run.json>, for the five meteor runs (self-test, solenoid-test, switch-test, coin-bookkeeping, gameplay) and one variant run each of meteora, meteorb, meteorbf, meteorc, meteord and meteorfp. ROM archives: meteor ee849e28a5edd2832012c433e6e71713f8c8773c874139ea24bc6d4bb9529438, meteora 7feebe36b85a3742daf3d2282e3ea4b9c37471e487d076fb96899d145f0f3f15, meteorb 8df1732f9e9211396b6d3df71dd66b6ac573d1213c4274277f2ce524a5ac9d70, meteorbf d743bea66b310693638a51850feeb4c56671191baee0239e4e9f8b6f3580abf9, meteorc d8f572bb4e42ba16e2eddb0f846eabf2a94c112ed48c63f183ae038722ba0d27, meteord 97609378f403a6a8ac7d56eea6d4679a89f906c7f251378ab49cc03c6844798d, meteorfp c7b549daa9acdb8d220ee44a815f4384a51a836d9e5f8c6b1495a5133e1ea4fe. Each scenario starts with a 25 s wait for the ROM's power-up test. Each set_switch or pulse is a host stimulus, never a ROM observation; display readings are seven-segment words read as digits.

coin-bookkeeping.note: Coin input 1 is closed once, coin input 2 twice and coin input 3 three times at PinMAME's default option switches (S20 and S21 ON, the rest OFF). The credit display read after each coin: 01, 02, 04, 05, 05, 05 (maximum-credits switches 17-19 OFF cap credits at 5). Sixteen Self Test presses then reach the bookkeeping functions; the match/ball-in-play display shows the function number and player 1 its count: function 09 -> 1, function 10 -> 2, function 11 -> 3. Every frame read is pinned in the frame-readings seed.

gameplay.note: A credited game on the single-ball outhole: each scoring switch is closed alone, each three-target bank is held down and raised, the six-target METEOR bank is held down in order M to R and raised, both flipper buttons are pressed, the ball drains, ball 2 is tilted, ball 3 drains to end the game, and a second game is started and slammed. Knock-down coils are not answered, so a target the ROM spots is never seen down. Each METEOR target held down puts out its own drop lamp (M 58, first E 42, T 26, second E 10, O 57; the sixth, R, completes the bank and relights them). At the first drain the drop lamps of T, second E, O, R were out, and the ROM fired exactly those targets' knock-down coils [8, 11, 12, 14] around the serve: the bank's memory. After the last drain the outhole kicker does not fire; public 19 drops and 45 and 63 light. Player 1's final score 539740 ends in the match number 40, the credits go from 02 to 03, and the knocker (6) fires once: a match award (option switch 21, ON at PinMAME's default). The scenario labels the tilted ball's serve step as bonus collection; the manual says a tilt forfeits the bonus, and the step observes only the serve. The four continuous lines are pulsed together at 6.39 s and 228.72 s (power-up, and the slam); public 18 is on 6.39-6.46 s; 8.90-222.37 s; 228.72-228.79 s; 231.23 s to the end and public 19 6.39-6.46 s; 33.51-161.93 s; 172.45-183.15 s; 211.21-222.37 s; 228.72-228.79 s; 242.68 s to the end. Every lamp address this run drives (56) is listed as driven outside the self test.

meteora-variant-io.note: The meteora ROM set on the same hardware: a credited game, the thumper, both slingshots, the stand-up target, the right three-bank held down and raised, both flipper buttons, a drain and the next serve. The four continuous lines are pulsed together once, at 6.39 s. Every step before the drain fires the same set of solenoids as the same step of the meteor gameplay run (sets compared; firing order, timing and lamp changes are not). The drain and the next serve taken together fire the outhole kicker (15) and the bank resets 3, 7, 9, 13 as in meteor, though not in the same windows: meteor fires them before the served ball leaves the outhole and only target restores after it, this run fires them again after it. No METEOR target switch closed in this run (the harness does not drop a target when the ROM fires its knock-down coil), and no knock-down coil fired at the drain or the serve; meteor's run, with four METEOR targets down, also restored those four there.

self-test.limitation: The burn-in drives the displays with test frames, so the driver numbers are read from the solenoid-test run instead.
self-test.note: One Self Test press starts the burn-in test. All sixty lamp addresses (60 seen) are driven and the four decoder holes 16, 32, 48 and 64 never are; the solenoids fire in a repeating 19-step cycle that starts with public 1.

solenoid-test.note: Four Self Test presses start the solenoid test, which pulses one driver at a time and shows its number on the player displays (read 0.25 s after each pulse; every frame read is pinned in the frame-readings seed). The ROM accepted every press. Over 4 complete cycles, driver numbers 1-19 pair with public addresses 1->2, 2->1, 3->6, 4->7, 5->3, 6->4, 7->5, 8->8, 9->11, 10->12, 11->14, 12->13, 13->9, 14->10, 15->19, 16->15, 17->17, 18->20, 19->18.

source.manifest_algorithm: source.sha256 is a directory manifest digest, not a file hash: list every file below source.path as {path, size, sha256} with path relative and POSIX-separated, sort by path, serialise as compact canonical JSON (indent=None, separators=(',',':'), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False), encode UTF-8 and take the SHA-256. At capture time the tree held 66 files totalling 13219828 bytes. Individual run hashes are in runtime.raw_runs[].sha256.
